findings.location: tools/codesign/tests/test-runner-image.sh: case 'the real runner starts with the registration in place' (docker logs -f loop)
findings.obligation: Fast loop: oracle finishes well under a minute after build; case 5 real run.sh
findings.observation: Non-blocking. The read loop breaks on a stop phrase but the process-substitution docker logs -f keeps running, so the case waits until the 60 s timeout or container exit even after a decisive line was seen; stop phrases (Must configure, Permission denied) are from memory and unrun against the real binary, and the tarball sha256 check in the design is not observed (build-time, outside expected (1)).
findings.remediation: After the break, docker rm -f the container (kills the log stream) and confirm the phrases once against the built image when implementation exists; optional: none required for craft.

findings.location: tools/codesign/tests/test-runner-image.sh: fill_registered_volume (.credentials_rsaparams '{}') and case 'the real runner starts with the registration in place'
findings.obligation: Expected (5): real run.sh started by the entrypoint prints neither Must configure nor Permission denied (network/auth failure acceptable)
findings.observation: Non-blocking. With the {} rsaparams fixture the real runner stops on 'An error occurred: Member d was not found' at credential parse, before network or auth. The case still catches an unregistered, symlinked or unwritable run directory (Must configure / Permission denied come first), so the promised falsifiers stay red, but it does not prove the runner gets as far as contacting GitHub.
findings.remediation: Optional: write a structurally valid RSAParameters JSON (d, dp, dq, exponent, inverseQ, modulus, p, q, base64) as the fixture so the runner reaches the network failure; not required for craft or completion.

observations.text: Re-review of uncommitted delta (git diff of test-runner-image.sh vs HEAD): chmod 644 added only inside the stand-ins run.sh, config.sh, curl and stale-run.sh, each on its own /record file (fixture output only; entrypoint/production umask untouched). record_of now prints 'unreadable=NAME' plus a stderr note when the record exists but cat fails, instead of aborting under set -e. Weakening check: an unreadable record yields no realdir/arg/version/curl-input values, so the owning checks (registered/older/register cases) still fail by name; recorded() still uses -f so the 'never started' checks are unchanged; a missing record still returns empty as before. Residual theoretical gap only if curl-argv alone were unreadable while curl-inputs stayed readable; both get one chmod line so not constructible. Designer evidence (uid 1001 run green; HEAD reproduces CI abort; chmod removed gives one named FAIL, no abort) accepted; not rerun by me.

diagnostic: Delta re-approved: fixture-only chmod, unreadable record fails its check by name, no check weakened. No new findings.
